title: (java) 백준 10971번 - 외판원 순회 2
partialText:
https://www.acmicpc.net/problem/10971

문제

> 외판원 순회 문제는 영어로 Traveling Salesman problem (TSP) 라고 불리는 문제로 computer science 분야에서 가장 중요하게 취급되는 문제 중 하나이다.
> 여러 가지 변종 문제가 있으나, 여기서는 가장 일반적인 형태의 문제를 살펴보자.

> 1번부터 N번까지 번호가 매겨져 있는 도시들이 있고, 도시들 사이에는 길이 있다.(길이 없을 수도 있다) 
> 이제 한 외판원이 어느 한 도시에서 출발해 N개의 도시를 모두 거쳐 다시 원래의 도시로 돌아오는 순회 여행 경로를 계획하려고 한다. 
> 단, 한 번 갔던 도시로는 다시 갈 수 없다. (맨 마지막에 여행을 출발했던 도시로 돌아오는 것은 예외) 
> 이런 여행 경로는 여러 가지가 있을 수 있는데, 가장 적은 비용을 들이는 여행 계획을 세우고자 한다.

> 각 도시간에 이동하는데 드는 비용은 행렬 W[i][j]형태로 주어진다.
> W[i][j]는 도시 i에서 도시 j로 가기 위한 비용을 나타낸다. 
> 비용은 대칭적이지 않다. 
> 즉, W[i][j] 는 W[j][i]와 다를 수 있다. 
> 모든 도시간의 비용은 양의 정수이다. W[i][i]는 항상 0이다. 
> 경우에 따라서 도시 i에서 도시 j로 갈 수 없는 경우도 있으며 이럴 경우 W[i][j]=0이라고 하자.

> N과 비용 행렬이 주어졌을 때, 가장 적은 비용을 들이는 외판원의 순회 여행 경로를 구하는 프로그램을 작성하시오.

접근

백트래킹으로 모든 점에서 시작하는 경우를 따지면서 일단 시작점을 기록해놓고 경우를 따진다. 모든 도시를 방문하면 앞서 기록한 시작점으로 다시 돌아가기 위해 마지막 지점에서 시작점까지의 비용을 더한 뒤 최소 비용을 계산한다.

문제해결

> 도시의 수를 N, 도시 간 비용을 cost 배열, 도시의 방문처리를 visited배열, 최종 비용을 answer로 선언한다.
> 도시의 수를 입력받고 cost배열, visited배열의 크기를 정의해주고 visited를 false로 초기화한다.
> 각 도시 간 비용을 입력받아 cost에 저장한다.
> 1번 도시부터 시작점으로 잡고 방문처리를 한 뒤 도시를 순회하는 백트래킹 함수 Salesman으로 들어간다. 
> 탐색이 끝나면 다른 경우를 위해 방문처리를 되돌린다.
> Salesman은 매개변수로 최초시작점, 직전에 방문한 곳, 지금까지의 비용, 총 방문한 도시의 수를 가진다.
> 매 재귀마다 1부터 N도시까지 보는데 방문처리가 안된 도시만 따진다.
> 그리고 만약 prev 즉, 직전 도시에서 이번에 가기로 뽑은 i도시까지의 비용이 0이면 못가므로 넘어간다.
> 가능한 도시를 뽑으면 방문처리하고 total에 비용을 더해주며 rst도 증가시켜 재귀로 넘긴다.
> 위 과정을 반복하며 rst가 N-1이 되면 모든 도시를 방문한것이므로 다시 시작점으로 돌아가야한다.
> 이때 prev에서 i가는 비용이 0이면 못간다 즉, 시작 도시로 다시 못돌아가므로 끝내준다.
> total에 돌아가는 비용을 더해 최종비용 answer과 최소값 연산으로 최소 비용을 갱신한다.

코드

import java.io.*;
import java.util.*;
import java.lang.*;

public class Main {
    //10971번 외판원 순회 2
    static int N;
    static int[][] cost;
    static boolean[] visited;
    static int answer = Integer.MAX_VALUE;
    static void Salesman(int start,int prev, int total, int rst) {
        if(rst == N - 1) {
            if(cost[prev][start] == 0) return;
            answer = Math.min(answer, total + cost[prev][start]);
            return;
        }
        for(int i = 1; i <= N; i++) {
            if(visited[i]) continue;
            if(cost[prev][i] == 0) continue;
            visited[i] = true;
            Salesman(start, i, total + cost[prev][i],rst + 1);
            visited[i] = false;
        }
    }
    public static void main(String[] args) throws IOException {
        BufferedReader br = new BufferedReader(new InputStreamReader(System.in));
        StringTokenizer st;
        N = Integer.parseInt(br.readLine());
        cost = new int[N+1][N+1];
        visited = new boolean[N+1];
        Arrays.fill(visited, false);

        for(int i = 1; i <= N; i++) {
            st = new StringTokenizer(br.readLine());
            for(int j = 1; j <= N; j++) cost[i][j] = Integer.parseInt(st.nextToken());
        }

        for(int i = 1; i <= N; i++) {
            visited[i] = true;
            Salesman(i, i, 0, 0);
            visited[i] = false;
        }
        System.out.print(answer);
    }
}

title: Smoker Trailer: The Ultimate Guide for BBQ Businesses and Catering Success
partialText:
If you're planning to start a BBQ business or expand your outdoor cooking capabilities, investing in a smoker trailer can be a game-changer. Designed for mobility, high-capacity cooking, and authentic smoky flavor, smoker trailers are widely used by professional pitmasters, caterers, and food truck owners.

In this guide, we’ll walk you through everything you need to know about smoker trailers—from benefits and types to buying tips and maintenance—so you can make the right investment for your business.

What Is a Smoker Trailer? A smoker trailer is a portable BBQ cooking unit mounted on a trailer, allowing you to cook large quantities of meat while moving from one location to another. These units typically use wood or charcoal as fuel and are designed to deliver slow-cooked, smoky flavors that define authentic barbecue.

Smoker trailers come in different sizes and configurations, making them suitable for food vendors, catering companies, BBQ competitions, and restaurants that require outdoor cooking solutions.

Why Choose a Smoker Trailer for Your Business? 1. Mobility and Flexibility

One of the biggest advantages of a smoker trailer is its portability. Whether you’re catering an event, setting up at a festival, or operating a mobile BBQ business, a smoker trailer allows you to cook and serve food anywhere.

  1. High Cooking Capacity

Smoker trailers are built for volume. You can cook large quantities of brisket, ribs, chicken, and more at once, making them ideal for commercial use.

  1. Authentic BBQ Flavor

Nothing beats the taste of slow-smoked meat. A smoker trailer uses real wood or charcoal, giving your food that rich, smoky flavor customers love.

  1. Cost-Effective Expansion

Compared to building a full restaurant kitchen, investing in a smoker trailer is a more affordable way to start or expand a BBQ business.

Types of Smoker Trailers Understanding the different types of smoker trailers will help you choose the right one for your needs.

Offset Smoker Trailer This is the most common type. It features a firebox attached to the main cooking chamber, allowing indirect heat and smoke to cook the meat evenly.

Best for: Traditional BBQ lovers and pitmasters

Reverse Flow Smoker Trailer In this design, heat and smoke travel under a plate before circulating back over the food, ensuring even cooking.

Best for: Consistent temperature control and uniform cooking

Vertical Smoker Trailer These smokers use vertical racks, maximizing space and allowing you to cook more food in a smaller footprint.

Best for: High-capacity cooking with limited space

Pellet Smoker Trailer Pellet smokers use wood pellets and automated controls to maintain consistent temperatures.

Best for: Beginners or businesses looking for convenience

Key Features to Look for in a Smoker Trailer

When buying a smoker trailer, it’s important to consider the features that will impact performance and efficiency.

Build Quality

Look for heavy-duty steel construction. A well-built smoker retains heat better and lasts longer.

Cooking Area

Choose a smoker trailer with enough cooking space to meet your business demands. Consider future growth as well.

Temperature Control

Good airflow design and adjustable vents are essential for maintaining consistent temperatures.

Storage and Prep Space

Some smoker trailers come with storage compartments, prep tables, and sinks, making them more functional for commercial use.

Mobility and Trailer Design

Ensure the trailer is easy to tow and complies with local regulations. Check for durable wheels, suspension, and hitch systems.

How to Choose the Right Smoker Trailer Selecting the perfect smoker trailer depends on your business goals and budget.

Define Your Purpose

Are you catering events, running a food truck, or competing in BBQ contests? Your use case will determine the size and type of smoker trailer you need.

Consider Your Budget

Smoker trailers can range from a few thousand to tens of thousands of dollars. Decide on a budget that balances quality and affordability.

Evaluate Fuel Type

Wood and charcoal provide traditional flavor, while pellet smokers offer convenience. Choose based on your cooking style.

Check Local Regulations

Before purchasing, make sure your smoker trailer complies with health and safety regulations in your area.

Benefits of Using a Smoker Trailer for Catering

If you're in the catering business, a smoker trailer offers several advantages:

On-site cooking for freshness and flavor Ability to serve large crowds efficiently Enhanced customer experience with live BBQ cooking Flexibility to operate at different venues

These benefits make smoker trailers a popular choice for weddings, corporate events, and festivals.

Maintenance Tips for Smoker Trailers

To ensure your smoker trailer performs well and lasts for years, proper maintenance is essential.

Clean After Every Use

Remove grease, ash, and food residue to prevent buildup and maintain hygiene.

Season the Smoker

Regularly season your smoker to protect it from rust and improve flavor.

Inspect for Damage

Check for leaks, cracks, or worn-out parts and fix them promptly.

Store Properly

When not in use, keep your smoker trailer covered and protected from the elements.

Is a Smoker Trailer Worth the Investment? Absolutely. A smoker trailer is not just a cooking tool—it’s a business asset. It allows you to expand your reach, increase your cooking capacity, and deliver high-quality BBQ wherever your customers are.

Whether you're starting a new BBQ venture or upgrading your current setup, a smoker trailer provides the flexibility and performance needed to succeed in a competitive market.

Smoker Trailer A smoker trailer is a powerful investment for anyone serious about BBQ. With its mobility, high capacity, and ability to produce authentic smoked flavors, it opens up countless opportunities in catering, food trucks, and outdoor events.

Before making a purchase, take the time to understand your needs, explore different types, and choose a model that aligns with your business goals. With the right smoker trailer, you’ll be well on your way to serving mouthwatering BBQ and growing a successful food business.
